Phoropter-tui rebuilt its fixtures at selvage's head (selvage put in markup what the pages said in prose) and answered selvage's guess: six of seven gaps closed, and the seventh only half. codeStart numbers an excerpt, but each line's number is still a span.ln inside the code property, so a microdata reader gets the numbers run into the code. Selvage's as-built is pushed and frozen, so the answer lands here.

Decision: Line numbers are drawn by a CSS counter, not written into the code

where src/render.ts file page

quote const text = `<span class="ln">${n}</span>${esc(line) || ' '}`;

Because (phoropter-tui's brief): code should hold the code. Each line becomes its own element, and a counter started from the excerpt's first line draws its number in ::before. A person sees what they see now; the code property's text is just the lines; copying an excerpt no longer copies its numbers. The brief's other options were a numbered attribute shown through CSS, or a profile line saying each line starts with its number; the counter keeps code true to its name, and the line number is already a property, codeStart.

Decision: Two excerpts in one view are ruled apart again

where src/style.css file page

quote .view pre + pre { border-top: 1px dashed var(--rule); }

Because (Claude, measured): selvage put a codeStart meta before each pre, so no pre directly follows another and the rule between excerpts stopped drawing. Nobody reported it; it showed up reading the stylesheet for this plan.
